1 أَثَّ , aor.
اَثِ3َ (T, S, M, L, K) and
اَثُ3َ and َ, (M, L, K,) inf. n. أَثَاثَةٌ(T, S, M, L, K) and أَثَاثٌ(M, L, K) and أُثُوثَةٌ, (M,) or أُثُوُثٌ, (L, K,) It (anything) was, or became, much in quantity, abundant, or numerous: and great, or large: (M, L:) it (herbage, or a herb,) was, or became, abundant, or plenteous, and tangled, or luxuriant; (T, S, K;) or abundant and tall: (M:) it (hair) was, or became, abundant and long. (M, TA.) ―
-b2- أَثَّتْ, (M, K,) aor.
اَثُ3َ , inf. n. أَثٌّ, (M,) said of a woman, She was, or became, large in the hinder parts. (M, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
